content.text: The Shaw family’s joyful Winton summer centers on the “S. W. F. Club,” whose outings, picnics, photography, and generosity revive Hilary and unite villagers, including Sextoness Jane. Uncle Paul visits the parsonage, reconciles with his brother, and offers Pauline and Hilary schooling. The narrative then shifts to Forbes-Mitchell’s recollections of the 1857 Indian Mutiny: British forces advance through Lucknow, storm the Dilkoosha, Martiniere, Secundrabagh, Shah Nujeef, Begum’s Kothee, and Kaiserbagh, relieve and evacuate the Residency, march to Cawnpore, defeat the Gwalior Contingent, pursue rebels through Bithoor and Futtehghur, and return to Lucknow. It recounts battlefield heroism, Hodson’s death, harsh reprisals, concealed gunpowder, looting, and soldiers’ personal anecdotes.
